tess: Quick note: onboarding user hit weird 408/timeouts in Android sample when using our Retrofit interceptor for auth. Steps: fresh install, sign-in, call generate -> sometimes hangs then times out.

omar: Any stack or how you build the client? interceptor order matters.

tess: We add AuthInterceptor then RetryInterceptor then LoggingInterceptor. Retrofit builder uses default callTimeout 0. Observed that cancelling coroutine doesn't cancel underlying OkHttp call sometimes.

lucy: Coroutine cancellation requires Call.cancel() in adapter. Our retrofit call adapter has a small bug: it transforms cancellation into IOException but doesn't call call.cancel() if using suspend wrapper. That explains stale connections piling up and eventual 408s.

tess: Repro: open sample, background app, reauth triggered (401) while streaming; cancellation occurred on UI side but underlying call stayed open, exhausting dispatcher threads.

omar: Two fixes: 1) ensure our CallAdapter invokes call.cancel() on coroutine cancellation; 2) move RetryInterceptor after AuthInterceptor so retries use fresh auth headers. Also set readTimeout longer for streaming calls and callTimeout lower for short requests.

lucy: Will send small patch changing adapter and update sample README to call out interceptor ordering, recommended timeouts, and how to disable automatic retries in Android.

ci-bot: CI scheduled for branch fix/android-retrofit-cancel (build #4901).

tess: Also add a short troubleshooting section in quickstart: "stuck requests? check coroutine cancellation, interceptor order, and connection pool". That will cut down onboarding Slack DMs.

omar: Good. Also add an integration test on emulator that cancels mid-stream and asserts call.cancel() invoked.

lucy: Opening PRs now.

tess: thanks!
